_meta.description: Return-to-Sport (RTS) timelines and criteria for common sports injuries. All data sourced from PubMed-indexed peer-reviewed literature. PMIDs cited for each entry.
_meta.note: Timelines represent consensus estimates from systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Individual variation is expected. Always apply criteria-based clearance alongside time-based guidelines.

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Grade I (minor – <10% fiber disruption, full ROM, mild pain)

rts_timeline.notes: Grade I average RTP 7.4 days in elite track athletes (Malliaropoulos et al., 2010)

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS ≤1/10 during sport-specific movements at full speed
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Hamstring:Quadriceps ratio ≥60% (concentric); eccentric hamstring strength ≥90% limb symmetry index (LSI)
functional_tests: Pain-free jogging progressing to full sprint
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Athlete self-reports confidence ≥7/10 in ACL-RSI analog item

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Grade II recurrence rate 24.1% within 24 months vs 9.3% Grade I (PMID 21051422); premature RTP is the primary modifiable recurrence risk factor

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Grade II (moderate – 10–50% fiber disruption, restricted ROM, palpable defect possible)

rts_timeline.notes: Average 12.9 days in elite athletes; recreational athletes average 3–6 weeks

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10 during maximal sprint, change-of-direction, and Nordic curl
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Eccentric hamstring LSI ≥90%; H:Q ratio ≥60% at 60°/s isokinetic
functional_tests: Sprint at 100% perceived effort without compensation
Change of direction at full speed (5-10-5 drill)
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Athlete self-reports readiness; no fear of re-injury at full speed

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Grade II shows highest recurrence rates (24.1% at 24 months); L-protocol eccentric exercises reduce reinjury rate (MD −1.95, PMID 40954668)

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Grade III (severe – >50% fiber disruption or complete rupture)

rts_timeline.notes: Average 29.5–55 days in elite athletes (Grades III–IV); severe injuries require imaging clearance

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10 at maximal exertion; MRI confirmation of structural healing at minimum 4 weeks
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Eccentric hamstring LSI ≥90%; isokinetic peak torque symmetry ≥85%
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Structured psychological readiness assessment; kinesiophobia screening (TSK-11 <37)

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Lower absolute recurrence in high-grade vs Grade II but catastrophic if re-ruptured; MRI guidance reduces premature RTP

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Complete tear requiring surgical reconstruction (BPTB or hamstring autograft)

rts_timeline.notes: APKASS 2024 consensus discourages purely time-based RTP; 9–12 months most evidence-supported. Youth athletes (≤18) may require 14–16 months (PMID 42077697)

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10 at all activities; no effusion
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Quadriceps LSI ≥90% (isokinetic at 60°/s); H:Q ratio ≥55–62.5%; LSI ≥90% required on isokinetic testing to pass battery (PMID 27423208)
functional_tests: Lachman test negative / Pivot shift negative
Full range of motion equal bilaterally
Sport-specific agility (cutting, pivoting) without pain or guarding
Bilateral drop-landing with symmetric knee flexion mechanics
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: ACL-RSI score ≥65 (optimal ≥70 associated with OR 2.1–2.5 for successful RTS, PMID 40894294); TSK-11 <37; fear of reinjury addressed via education and graded exposure

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: ACL graft rupture 10%, contralateral ACL rupture 8% at 5 years in soccer population; risk 3–7× higher in athletes ≤18 vs >25 (PMID 36190172). 44% of males ≤18 sustained further ACL injury

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Complete tear in athlete ≤18 years with open physes

rts_timeline.notes: Average 9–12 months; younger athletes may require 14–16 months (PMID 42077697)

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10; radiographic physeal closure or surgeon clearance
functional_tests: Gapski-Goodman or ImPACT-style sport-specific tests if concussion history
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: ACL-RSI ≥65; parental and coaching team involved in decision; graduated sport exposure

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Highest risk group – 3–7× increased graft rupture vs adults >25 years

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Grade I (mild – ATFL stretched, no rupture)

rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Ankle eversion/inversion strength deficit <15% vs contralateral
functional_tests: Single-leg balance 30 seconds (eyes open and closed)
Star Excursion Balance Test (SEBT) reach ≥90% of contralateral
Hopping and jogging without antalgic gait
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Ankle instability self-report minimal; willing to play without brace dependency

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Early mobilization superior to immobilization; functional bracing during return reduces reinjury; 6–12 months bracing during sport prevents recurrence (PMID 29671490)

rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Grade II (moderate – partial ATFL rupture, possible CFL involvement)

rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Evertor:invertor strength ratio symmetric; peroneals ≥90% LSI
functional_tests: Running and cutting without bracing dependency (long-term)
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Fear of reinjury addressed; ankle confidence self-report ≥8/10

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Previous lateral ankle sprain is top predictor of recurrence; functional rehab required before full RTS (PMID 41385332)

rts_timeline.notes: Some require surgical stabilization (Brostrom); post-surgical timeline 4–6 months

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10; no mechanical instability on talar tilt/anterior drawer
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Confidence with rapid direction change; no habitual bracing dependency

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Incomplete ligament healing leads to chronic ankle instability if RTS premature

rts_timeline.notes: Small-medium tears typically 4–6 months; large/massive tears 9–12 months. Overhead throwers often require 12 months (PMID 37588949)

rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Rotator cuff strength ≥90% LSI; external rotation:abduction strength ratio within normal
functional_tests: Full pain-free ROM (forward flexion, IR, ER, abduction)
Closed kinetic chain upper extremity stability test
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Confidence with overhead loading; no pain anticipation

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Premature loading during early repair phase leads to re-tear (failure rates 20–40% if non-compliant); protecting tissue for first 6 weeks critical (PMID 37588949)

rts_timeline.notes: Conservative: 3–6 months; surgical (if refractory): 6–12 months. Fat pad debridement adds 7-week delay (PMID 41553011)

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS ≤2/10 during jumping and landing (Victorian Institute of Sports Assessment – Patellar [VISA-P] score ≥80)
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Eccentric quad strength (decline squat) equal bilaterally; single-leg decline squat pain-free
functional_tests: Sport-specific jumping volume without pain flare >24h post-activity
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Understanding of load management; kinesiophobia screened; graduated sport exposure

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Load-related flare-up risk if VISA-P <70 at RTS; tendon not pain-free under load is primary risk factor

rts_timeline.notes: Heavy slow resistance loading (HSR) protocol 12 weeks minimum; progression to sport 3–12 months based on severity

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS ≤2/10 during single-leg calf raises and running; no post-activity flare >24h
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Single-leg calf raise repetitions ≥90% contralateral; calf raise endurance matched
functional_tests: 25 single-leg calf raises at bodyweight pain-free
Single-leg triple hop for distance LSI ≥90%
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Load monitoring understanding; graduated running plan adhered to

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Premature running loads without tendon capacity causes re-irritation; 40–60% require >6 months

rts_timeline.notes: 65–100% return to sport between 3–13.4 months; mean 7 months in surgical cohorts (PMID 37235667). Re-rupture rate 0–5.74%

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: NRS 0/10 at full running and single-leg activities
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Calf peak torque ≥90% contralateral; limb symmetry on hop tests ≥90%
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Fear of re-rupture addressed; graduated RTS protocol completed

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Re-rupture 0–5.74%; functional outcome highly dependent on adherence to staged return (PMID 37235667)

rts_timelines.injury_name: Stress Fracture – Low Risk (Metatarsal shaft, fibula, medial tibia)
rts_timelines.grade_or_severity: Low-risk location: metatarsal shaft (2–4), fibula, medial tibia

rts_timeline.notes: Most stress fractures heal in 6–8 weeks; rate of resumption guided by symptoms (PMID 9421865)

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: Pain-free at fracture site on palpation and activity
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Functional strength and proprioception restored; no limping
functional_tests: Progressive running program: walk→jog→run→sprint over 4–6 weeks
Hop test on affected limb pain-free
Return of sport-specific mechanics without compensation
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: Athlete understands load management; training error identified and corrected

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Progression to displaced fracture or non-union if loading resumed too early; female athletes with menstrual disturbances at higher risk (PMID 9421865)

rts_timelines.injury_name: Stress Fracture – High Risk (Femoral neck, anterior tibia cortex, navicular, 5th metatarsal)

rts_timeline.notes: Femoral neck, anterior tibia cortex, navicular, 2nd and 5th metatarsals: delayed union or non-union risk; some require surgery

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: Radiographic healing confirmed (CT or MRI) AND pain-free weight-bearing
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: No cortical defect on imaging; symmetrical lower limb mechanics
functional_tests: Progressive sport-specific return over 4–6 weeks after imaging clearance

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Femoral neck displaced fractures are surgical emergencies; non-union of navicular requires screw fixation. Risk of catastrophic failure if RTS premature

rts_timeline.notes: Stepwise protocol – each stage minimum 24h. Pediatric athletes require additional caution and physician clearance. Complex concussion may require weeks–months

rts_criteria.pain_threshold: Complete symptom resolution at rest; SCAT5 score within normal limits
rts_criteria.strength_criteria: Not applicable for typical concussion; neurological examination normal
functional_tests: Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity (daily activities that do not provoke symptoms)
Stage 2: Light aerobic exercise (walking, swimming – no resistance training)
Stage 3: Sport-specific exercise (skating drills, running – no head impact)
Stage 4: Non-contact training drills (passing drills, complex agility)
Stage 5: Full-contact practice after medical clearance
ImPACT or neurocognitive testing within normal limits
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: No anxiety or depression; sleep quality monitored (sleep disturbance post-SRC is common – PMID 34145161)

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Second Impact Syndrome (catastrophic brain swelling) documented in youth athletes who sustain second concussion before full recovery; symptomatic RTS is strictly contraindicated

rts_timelines.injury_name: General Muscle Strain (Quadriceps, Calf, Groin / Adductor)
rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: 20–30% recurrence risk in general muscle strains without criteria-based clearance

rts_timelines.injury_name: General Muscle Strain (Quadriceps, Calf, Groin / Adductor)

functional_tests: Agility and change of direction pain-free
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: No fear of re-injury; graduated return under supervision

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Without eccentric strengthening, re-injury risk is elevated; eccentric protocols significantly reduce recurrence (PMID 40954668)

rts_timeline.notes: RTS timelines range <6 to 12 months across studies; limited standardization (PMID 41811648)

rts_criteria.strength_criteria: LSI ≥90% quadriceps and hamstring; isokinetic testing recommended; IKDC >90 and Lysholm >85
functional_tests: Full ROM extension and near-full flexion
rts_criteria.psychological_clearance: ACL-RSI analog; confidence with pivoting and contact

rts_timelines.re_injury_risk_if_early: Re-instability and chronic PCL laxity if RTS without full strength and ROM recovery (PMID 41811648)
